mainTopic: חזקה on the land of a בורח, whether a מחאה made away from the possessor counts, and what wording makes a valid מחאה
overview: The amud opens by finishing an answer about our משנה: the normal situation between יהודה and גליל is treated like a time of crisis. רב יהודה then reports in the name of רב that one cannot make a חזקה on the land of a בורח, and שמואל objects that a protest does not need to be made face to face. The גמרא asks how רב can say this, since רב himself holds that a protest away from the possessor counts. It answers that רב was only explaining the reason of the תנא of our משנה. In a second version, רב says one CAN make a חזקה on a בורח's land, and שמואל calls this obvious. The גמרא explains that רב's real point is that a protest counts even before two people who cannot tell the possessor, because word passes from friend to friend, while שמואל disagrees. רבא then rules that there is no חזקה on a בורח's land and that a protest away from the possessor is valid. He settles the clash by splitting the cases: someone who fled over money versus someone who fled a death charge. Finally, the גמרא asks what words make a valid protest, and רב זביד begins to answer; his ruling continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Normal times between Judea and Galilee count like a crisis
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes explaining our משנה: the usual situation between יהודה and גליל is treated like שעת חירום.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because ordinary travel between Judea and the Galilee is treated like a time of crisis.
steps.whatsHappening: This line finishes an answer that started earlier on the daf. It explains why our משנה says a חזקה does not work when the owner is in one region and the possessor is in the other.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תנא of the משנה treats the normal situation between יהודה and גליל as if it were a time of crisis. In a crisis, the owner's protest is not expected to reach the possessor, so his silence proves nothing. That is why the possession does not count as a חזקה.

keyTerms.meaning: ordinary, the usual situation
a time of crisis or emergency, when travel and contact are cut off
they are like, they are treated as

phrases.english: That an ordinary situation between Judea and the Galilee
is like a time of crisis.

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּסְתַם יְהוּדָה וּגְלִיל, כִּשְׁעַת חֵירוּם דָּמוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes an answer begun before this section about the reasoning of our משנה.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpreting the reason behind the משנה
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה's rule comes from treating יהודה and גליל as cut off from each other, like in a crisis.

steps.title: רב: no presumption of ownership on a fugitive's land
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה quotes רב: a person cannot make a חזקה on the property of a בורח.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of רב: One cannot establish a presumption of ownership on the property of someone who has fled.
steps.whatsHappening: A new ruling is brought from רב: if the owner ran away, someone living on his land cannot claim it through חזקה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A חזקה works because the owner had a chance to protest and stayed silent. A בורח is not in a position to protest against the person on his land. So his silence proves nothing, and the possession does not count.

keyTerms.meaning: establish a חזקה, a presumption of ownership based on years of use
the property of
a person who fled, for example from danger or the government

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said that Rav said:
One cannot establish a presumption of ownership on the property of a fugitive.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new related topic: חזקה when the owner cannot easily protest.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: No חזקה can be made on a בורח's property.

steps.title: שמואל: the owner does not need to protest face to face
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה reports that when he told this to שמואל, שמואל objected: the owner does not have to protest in front of the possessor.
steps.simpleTranslation: When I said this in front of שמואל, he said to me: Does he really have to protest in his presence?!
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל challenges רב's ruling. A protest can be made anywhere, so even a fugitive can protest.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב's ruling seems to assume the owner must protest in front of the possessor, which a fugitive cannot do. שמואל rejects that assumption, because a protest made in front of witnesses elsewhere is enough. So the fugitive could have protested, his silence does mean something, and a חזקה should work.

keyTerms.meaning: I said it in front of him
to protest, to formally object to someone using your land
in his presence, face to face

phrases.aramaic: כִּי אַמְרִיתַהּ קַמֵּיהּ דִּשְׁמוּאֵל, אָמַר לִי:
phrases.english: When I said it before Shmuel, he said to me:
phrases.notes: The speaker here is רב יהודה, telling over what happened.

phrases.english: But does he need to protest in his presence?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the ruling of רב in step 2.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's ruling that no חזקה works on a בורח's property
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A protest does not need to be made in front of the possessor, so a fugitive can still protest, and a חזקה should work.

steps.title: רב seems to contradict himself
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: is רב teaching that a protest made away from the possessor does not count? But רב himself said it does count!
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב, what is he teaching us? That a protest not in his presence is not a protest? But didn't רב say: A protest not in his presence is a protest!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out a contradiction between two statements of רב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב's ruling about the בורח only makes sense if a protest must be made face to face. But elsewhere רב rules clearly that a protest made away from the possessor is valid. So how can both statements come from רב?

keyTerms.meaning: what is he teaching us?
a protest against someone using your land
but didn't he say? (introduces a contradiction)
is, counts as

phrases.english: And Rav, what is he teaching us?

phrases.aramaic: מֶחָאָה שֶׁלֹּא בְּפָנָיו לָא הָוְיָא מֶחָאָה?!
phrases.english: That a protest not in his presence is not a protest?!
But didn't Rav say:
A protest not in his presence is a protest!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on שמואל's point to show that רב contradicts himself.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רב himself holds that a protest away from the possessor counts, so he should allow a חזקה on a בורח's land.

steps.title: רב was only explaining our משנה's opinion
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers: רב was explaining the reasoning of the תנא of our משנה, but he himself does not agree with it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב was explaining the reason of the תנא of our משנה, but he himself does not hold this way.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא resolves the contradiction. The ruling about the בורח was not רב's own view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב said 'no חזקה on a בורח's property' only to explain how the תנא of our משנה rules. It was not his own opinion. רב's own view is that a protest made away from the possessor does count.

keyTerms.meaning: the reason
the תנא of our own משנה
he is explaining
he does not hold this way

steps.whatToRemember: In this version, רב's ruling against a חזקה on a בורח's property was only an explanation of our משנה. רב himself holds that a protest made away from the possessor is valid.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not think רב changed his mind or holds two opinions. He is simply explaining someone else's opinion here.

phrases.english: Rav was explaining the reason of the tanna of our Mishnah,
but he himself does not hold this way.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in step 4.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Attributing the statement to another opinion
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב's ruling about the בורח was his own view, which clashes with his other statement.
steps.terutzMaskana: רב was only explaining the תנא of our משנה, and he himself holds that a protest away from the possessor counts.

steps.title: Another version: רב allows presumption on a fugitive's land
steps.stepSummary: Some report רב's ruling the opposite way: one CAN make a חזקה on the property of a בורח.
steps.simpleTranslation: And there are those who say: רב יהודה said that רב said: One can establish a presumption of ownership on the property of a fugitive.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second version of רב's statement, in which רב says the opposite of the first version.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this version, רב holds that a חזקה DOES work on a בורח's land. This fits well with רב's other view that a protest made away from the possessor is valid. The fugitive could have protested from wherever he was, so his silence counts.

keyTerms.meaning: there are those who say (introduces a second version)

phrases.english: And there are those who say:
Rav Yehuda said that Rav said:
One can establish a presumption of ownership on the property of a fugitive.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second, opposite version of רב's ruling from step 2.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A חזקה can be made on a בורח's property.

steps.title: שמואל: that is obvious
steps.stepSummary: In this version, שמואל tells רב יהודה that רב's ruling is obvious, since the owner does not need to protest face to face.
steps.simpleTranslation: When I said this before שמואל, he said to me: That is obvious! Does he really have to protest in his presence?!
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל agrees with רב's ruling, but challenges why it even needed to be said.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here שמואל does not disagree with the law. He argues that it is obvious, because everyone knows a protest can be made away from the possessor. So of course a fugitive's silence counts, and a חזקה works.

keyTerms.meaning: it is obvious, why say it?

steps.whatToRemember: In both versions, שמואל holds that a protest does not have to be made face to face. The only question is what רב said: in the first version שמואל disagrees with רב, and in the second he calls רב's ruling obvious.

phrases.aramaic: כִּי אַמְרִיתַהּ קַמֵּיהּ דִּשְׁמוּאֵל, אֲמַר לִי:
phrases.english: When I said it before Shmuel, he said to me:
It is obvious!
Does he need to protest in his presence?!

steps.triggerLanguage: פְּשִׁיטָא! וְכִי לִמְחוֹת בְּפָנָיו הוּא צָרִיךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: שמואל responds to the second version of רב's ruling in step 6.
steps.kashyaTarget: The need for רב's ruling in the second version
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Since a protest does not need to be made face to face, it is obvious that a חזקה works on a בורח's land, so why say it?

steps.title: What is new in רב's ruling?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the second version of רב's ruling: if it only teaches that a protest away from the possessor counts, רב already said that once.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב, what is he teaching us? That a protest not in front of the possessor counts? But רב already said that once!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what רב's ruling in step 6 adds, since it seems to repeat something רב already taught.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the second version, רב said one CAN make a חזקה on a בורח's property, because the owner can protest from far away. But רב already ruled elsewhere that a מחאה שלא בפניו counts. So this ruling seems to teach nothing new.

keyTerms.meaning: What is he teaching us? (What is new here?)
One time (already said once)
A protest made away from the possessor

phrases.english: And Rav, what is he teaching us?
phrases.notes: This is רב in the second version (step 6), who said one CAN make a חזקה on a בורח's property.

phrases.english: That a protest not in his presence is a protest?!
But Rav already said it one time!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Picks up שמואל's remark in step 7 that רב's ruling is obvious, and asks what רב adds.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's ruling in step 6 that one can make a חזקה on a בורח's property
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ruling must teach something new. If the point is only that a protest away from the possessor counts, רב already said so.

steps.title: רב's new point: even witnesses who cannot pass it on
steps.stepSummary: רב's real חידוש is that a protest counts even in front of two people who cannot tell the possessor themselves.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, this is what he teaches us: even if the owner protested in front of two people who cannot tell the possessor, it still counts as a protest.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רב is teaching something new: the witnesses to the protest do not need to be people who can reach the possessor themselves.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The new point is not just that a protest away from the possessor counts. It is that even when the two listeners have no way to tell him, it still counts. This sets up a disagreement with שמואל, which the next step shows.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather (switching to a new explanation)
He protested
Who are unable to tell him

phrases.english: Rather, this is what he teaches us:
that even if he protested in front of two people
who cannot tell him,
phrases.notes: "Him" means the person living on the land, the one being protested against.

phrases.english: it is a protest.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 8 by giving רב's ruling a new point.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the חידוש: the ruling teaches a further point that goes beyond what רב said before
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב only meant that a protest away from the possessor counts, which he had already said.
steps.terutzMaskana: רב teaches that even a protest before witnesses who cannot reach the possessor counts.

steps.title: שמואל holds the witnesses must be able to tell him
steps.stepSummary: רב ענן reports from שמואל that a protest counts only before people who can tell the possessor. This shows that רב's point is really new.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רב ענן said: שמואל himself explained to me: if the owner protested in front of two people who can tell the possessor, it is a protest. If he protested in front of two people who cannot tell him, it is not a protest.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings שמואל's view, reported by רב ענן, to show that רב's ruling teaches something that others disagree with.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל draws a line: the listeners must be people who can actually pass the protest on to the possessor. So רב's ruling, that even listeners who cannot tell him are enough, is a real חידוש against שמואל.

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא, a student of שמואל
It was explained to me personally
Who are able to tell him

phrases.english: As Rav Anan said:
To me personally it was explained
by Mar Shmuel himself:
If he protested in front of two people
who can tell him, it is a protest;
if he protested in front of two people

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁאֵין יְכוֹלִין לוֹמַר לוֹ – לָא הָוְיָא מֶחָאָה.
phrases.english: who cannot tell him, it is not a protest.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאָמַר רַב עָנָן: לְדִידִי מִפָּרְשָׁא לִי מִינֵּיהּ דְּמָר שְׁמוּאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports step 9 by showing there is a real opinion, שמואל's, that disagrees with רב.
steps.raayaObject: That רב's ruling in step 9 is a real חידוש
steps.raayaSupportSource: שמואל's ruling as reported by רב ענן: listeners who cannot tell the possessor do not make a valid protest

steps.title: רב's reason: word spreads from friend to friend
steps.stepSummary: רב holds that even listeners who cannot reach the possessor will tell their friends, who tell their friends, until word reaches him.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב holds: your friend has a friend, and your friend's friend has a friend.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why רב disagrees with שמואל and counts the protest anyway.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב reasons that news spreads along a chain of friends. Even if the two listeners cannot tell the possessor themselves, the protest will reach him in the end. So the protest is enough to warn him to keep his documents.

keyTerms.meaning: Your friend has a friend (news spreads)
Your friend's friend

steps.whatToRemember: רב: a protest counts even before people who cannot reach the possessor, because word spreads. שמואל: the listeners must be able to tell him.

phrases.english: And Rav holds: your friend has a friend,
and your friend's friend has a friend.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains why רב rejects שמואל's requirement from step 10.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Giving the reasoning behind רב's position
steps.terutzHavaAmina: If the listeners cannot reach the possessor, he will never hear of the protest.
steps.terutzMaskana: News passes from friend to friend, so the protest will reach him.

steps.title: רבא's ruling on the בורח and on a protest made away from the possessor
steps.stepSummary: רבא rules that one cannot make a חזקה on a בורח's property, and that a protest made away from the possessor counts.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: the הלכה is that one cannot make a חזקה on the property of a בורח, and a protest made away from the possessor is a protest.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives the final הלכה on both questions discussed so far.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא rules two things: a בורח's land is protected from a חזקה, and a מחאה שלא בפניו is valid. The next step will ask how these two rulings fit together.

keyTerms.meaning: The halacha (final ruling)
One cannot make a חזקה
Property of someone who fled

phrases.english: Rava said: the halacha is:
one cannot make a chazakah on the property of one who fled,
and a protest not in his presence is a protest.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the רב and שמואל discussion to a final ruling of הלכה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: No חזקה on a בורח's property; a protest away from the possessor is valid.

steps.title: Aren't these two rulings contradictory?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how רבא can rule both ways: if a protest from afar counts, why can't one make a חזקה on a בורח's property?
steps.simpleTranslation: Two rulings? They contradict each other!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבא for saying two things that seem to clash.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a protest away from the possessor counts, then a בורח could protest from wherever he is. So there is no reason to stop a חזקה on his land. Saying both rulings seems contradictory.

keyTerms.meaning: Two (things that contradict)

phrases.english: Two?!
phrases.notes: How can רבא say both? If a far-away protest counts, the בורח could just protest from where he is.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the two halves of רבא's ruling in step 12.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The reason a בורח's land is protected is that he cannot protest. But if a protest from afar is valid, he can protest, so the protection makes no sense.

steps.title: Fleeing over money versus fleeing over a death charge
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the two rulings deal with different kinds of בורח: one who fled over money, and one who fled over a death charge.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is not difficult. Here, he fled because of money. There, he fled because of a death charge.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא resolves the contradiction by saying each ruling applies to a different case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Someone who fled because of money troubles can still protest from afar, so the rule that a far-away protest counts applies to him. Someone who fled from a death charge must stay hidden and cannot publicize a protest, so his land is protected from a חזקה.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not difficult
Because of money troubles
A death charge from the government

steps.whatToRemember: A בורח over money can protest from afar, so a חזקה works against him unless he protests. A בורח over a death charge cannot protest, so no חזקה works against him.

phrases.english: It is not difficult;
here, he is fleeing because of money;
there, he is fleeing because of a death charge.
phrases.notes: His life is in danger, so he must stay hidden and cannot let people know where he is by protesting.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא קַשְׁיָא; כָּאן בּוֹרֵחַ מֵחֲמַת מָמוֹן, כָּאן בּוֹרֵחַ מֵחֲמַת מְרָדִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in step 13.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Every בורח is in the same situation, so the two rulings clash.
steps.terutzMaskana: The money-fleer can protest from afar; the one fleeing a death charge cannot, so his land is protected.

steps.title: What wording counts as a protest?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens a new topic and asks what a valid protest must say.
steps.simpleTranslation: What does a protest look like?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up a new discussion about the exact words that make a valid מחאה. The answers come in the next steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Until now the question was where and in front of whom the protest is made. Now the question is its content. This opens a series of opinions.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the case? What does it look like?

phrases.english: What does a protest look like?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the בורח discussion and starts defining the wording of a protest.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What words make a protest valid

steps.title: רב זביד: a general insult is not enough
steps.stepSummary: רב זביד says that just calling someone a robber is not a protest. Saying he holds my land by robbery begins the valid version, and the ruling continues in the next part.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב זביד said: "So-and-so is a robber" is not a protest. "So-and-so is a robber, who holds my land through robbery"...
steps.whatsHappening: רב זביד starts answering by contrasting a vague accusation with one that names the land.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Calling someone a robber in general does not tell anyone that this land is being disputed, so it is not a protest. The second wording ties the robbery to the owner's land, and the ruling on it comes right after this part ends.

keyTerms.meaning: So-and-so
Robber
Through robbery

phrases.english: Rav Zevid said:
"So-and-so is a robber": it is not a protest.
"So-and-so is a robber,
since he holds my land through robbery,"

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב זְבִיד: פְּלָנְיָא גַּזְלָנָא הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins answering the question of step 15.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A general claim like "he is a robber" is not a protest; the protest must connect the robbery to the owner's land (ruling continues).
